name: Socialdemokraterna / Mona Sahlin (2010 joint S-MP-V motion)
detail: Motion 2009/10:Fi15 says reintroducing the old wealth tax in its earlier form is "inte helt realistiskt" and proposes a study of how tax on the wealthy can rise by about SEK 4bn. No wealth tax is named as a goal.

name: Niklas Karlsson m.fl. (S), motion 2022/23:2138
detail: Says the abolished wealth tax had a progressive distributional profile, and that the best-off should contribute more, but does not ask for a wealth tax.

name: Ida Gabrielsson (V)
detail: TV4 2026-05-18 quotes her as saying that whoever has most must contribute a little more; no wealth tax named in her own words. Covered through the party and the motion signatories.

name: Ameer Sachet (S), motion 2009/10:Sk342
detail: Calls for a wealth tax but was submitted in autumn 2009, before the 2010-01-01 window. Check for later statements.

name: Carl Schlyter (MP), motion 2017/18:2107
detail: "Ökade förmögenhetsskatter, arvsskatter samt marginalskatter" is rational, in a motion on top salaries. Already recorded through the 2017/18:2962 motion; keep as a possible second evidence row.

name: Förmögenhetsregister / förmögenhetsdeklaration motions (V, S 2013-2025)
detail: Motions asking for wealth statistics or a wealth declaration (e.g. 2013/14:Fi274 by S, 2020/21:2299 and 2021/22:2597 by V) are about information, not a tax.

name: Mikaela Valtersson (MP), 2011
detail: Said in the chamber on 2011-04-13: "Från Miljöpartiets sida kommer vi inte att driva frågan om förmögenhetsskatt." The party later changed line (motions 2013-2017 by individual MPs; party motion 2026). Context for the MP rows, not a supporter.

name: Socialdemokraterna leadership (Magdalena Andersson, Mikael Damberg, Mathias Tegnér), 2013-2025
detail: Rejected a wealth tax in the chamber and in answers: Damberg 2013-01-16 (no reintroduction), Andersson as finance minister 2015-03-25 ("Jag har inte tagit några sådana initiativ"), Damberg 2022-01-11 (no work under way), Tegnér 2024-03-19 ("nej, det är inte ett första steg mot en återinförd förmögenhetsskatt"). TV4 2026-05-18 reports that S does not go to the election on a billionaire tax. The party wants "de allra mest förmögna ska bidra mer" through other taxes. Re-check after the 2026 election.

name: Exit tax motions 2025/26 by S (Niklas Karlsson 2025/26:3554 yrkande 4) and V (Szatmári Waldau 2025/26:177 yrkande 10); interpellation 2025/26:548 by Mathias Tegnér (S)
detail: Call for an exit tax on unrealised gains when people emigrate, not tied to a wealth tax in the text read. Committee report 2025/26:SkU15 (reservation 7 by S, V, MP). Check in R003 whether any of the authors tie it to a wealth or billionaire tax; if so add under exit_tax.

name: Tankesmedjan Tiden, report 2020:5 "Skatten och kapitalet" (Bustos and Örjes)
detail: Underlag report for the labour movement tax inquiry; section 4.4 "Ingen ny förmögenhetsskatt": a wealth tax is attractive in theory but hard to implement. Recommends property, inheritance and gift taxes instead. The shadow inquiry did not take a position on the authors proposals. Tiden is now an actor: its 2017 report (no. 7) recommended a reintroduced wealth tax and the 2020 report is recorded as a retraction.

name: Katalys, report no. 75 "Beskatta kapitalet" (Sundgren, 2019)
detail: Novus poll of voters on a tax on fortunes over SEK 10m and a progressive property tax; the authors conclude a majority of voters support "en sådan reform" and that a redistributive reform raising capital taxation would be popular, but do not argue for a wealth tax in their own words. It cites LO as wanting inheritance, wealth and property taxes back. Check Daniel Suhonen (Katalys head) own articles in R004.

name: LO report "Förmögenhetsskatten" (Andersson and Löfgren, 2000s)
detail: LO-published study of who paid the wealth tax; undated in the PDF but ISBN 91-566-1467-5, before the abolition in 2007. Not evidence for the window.

name: Rättvisepartiet Socialisterna (Offensiv, socialisterna.org)
detail: Articles in the party paper note Oxfam's wealth-tax proposal and criticise S for rejecting a wealth tax and billionaire tax (2023-01-25, 2026-09-16) but do not state the party's own proposal in the pages read. Check the party programme.

name: Olof Johansson-Stenman (professor, University of Gothenburg)
detail: EFN, 2026-01-18: sees value in counteracting inequality and thinks incentive effects of a billionaire tax are not large, but says it is not very realistic because of capital mobility. Not a call for the tax. Re-check for his own articles.

name: Economists and business leaders opposing a billionaire tax, 2026 (Waldenström, Calmfors, F. N. G. Andersson, Jonung; Hagströmer, Wallenberg, Lundberg, Lorentzon, Tikkanen; DN leader writers Max Hjelm and the DN editorial board)
detail: Quoted against in EFN, Realtid, DN Debatt and Dagens PS pieces; recorded so they are not re-checked as supporters. Waldenström and Calmfors say wealth taxes raise little or nothing; Waldenström prefers taxing returns on capital. Read in full via the headless browser in R004: DN Debatt 2026-08-19 (Andersson and Jonung), 2026-08-31 (eight business leaders), Expressen Debatt 2026-09-05 (Lorentzon) and 2026-08-20 (Klas Tikkanen, Nordic Capital).

name: Thomas Östros (former S finance spokesperson)
detail: Realtid pages dated 2026 describe an Ekot interview where he wants to reintroduce a modern wealth tax, but the same pages recycle 2009-2014 coverage (Sahlin era), so the date is unreliable; a Sveriges Radio item on his 1% proposal is from 2009. No dated statement from 2010 or later found.

name: Sebastian Svahn (Malmö Arbetarekommun member)
detail: Author of motion 7 to the Skåne S district congress 2023 (reinstate capital tax and wealth tax), submitted through Malmö Arbetarekommun. A private party member; the district board response is not shown in the motion booklet.

name: Gunilla Berglund and Gitte Jutvik (V members, K26 motion E 102)
detail: Signed a congress e-motion for a billionaire tax for the climate; private party members, in a motion booklet.
